info.title: OpenGunstore API
info.description:
RPC API of the OpenGunstore custom apps (Frappe/ERPNext v16): ffl_core, ffl_integrations, ffl_woo_sync.

All endpoints are Frappe *whitelisted methods* invoked as `/api/method/<dotted.path>`. Unless an endpoint declares explicit HTTP verbs, it is documented here as POST (Frappe also accepts GET for read-only calls; always POST mutations). Arguments may be sent as JSON body, form data, or query string — JSON body is recommended.

Every operation carries an **Auth (derived from code)** line statically resolved from the role gate the function actually executes; the prose Permissions note adds semantics the machine can't infer.

Standard CRUD on DocTypes is served by Frappe's REST layer (`/api/resource/<DocType>`) — see docs/api/frappe-rest.md; the custom DocTypes are modelled under components.schemas and listed in reference/doctypes.md.

file go on the timeline. A missing signature can never be waived: without a

post.description:
Creates the customer's Pending copy of the template, or re-issues the one
already pending (its old link stops working and its text is rendered again).
While that copy still has a working link — the customer may be signing on the
tablet right now — nothing changes unless ``replace`` is 1: the answer is

200.description: {"name": the Customer Agreement, "deliver", "token_expires"} plus, for ``qr``, "sign_url" and "qr_svg" (an SVG data URI); for ``email``, "email". The link itself is never stored.

template.description: Agreement Template name; must be active.

deliver.description: ``tablet`` — send the link to a paired signing tablet (``terminal``; ``ffl_core.signing_terminal``), which opens it by itself once the request commits (a caller that never commits sends nothing); ``qr`` — return the signing link and a QR code for the counter; ``email`` — email the link to the customer (refused when the customer has no email address); ``none`` — only create the Pending copy (a manager then records a paper copy on it).

replace.description: 1 to re-issue even though the pending copy's link still works.

terminal.description: Signing Terminal name, for ``tablet``; must be active and paired.

serial_no.description: The gun, for an Each firearm sold template (it or *firearms* is required there).

price.description: The gun's price in this sale, for the text's ``{{ price }}``.

reference_doctype.description: For a Per document template (required there): the record's DocType.

reference_name.description: That record's name; the caller must be able to read it, and the record's ``agreement_context()`` fills the text's placeholders.

firearms.description: For an Each firearm sold template, several guns signed for at once: [{"serial_no", "price"}]. One copy covers them all (refused for a template with One copy per gun); a pending copy covering any of them is the one re-issued.

post.summary: Sign an agreement through a one-time link (Guest).
post.description:
Checked before anything is written: the "I agree" tick, the typed name, the
token (same error for every invalid one), the signature (a PNG of at most
500 KB and 2000 px with ink on it) and the age rule. A link opened as a QR
code at the counter, or on a paired signing tablet (its device key sent as
``terminal_secret``; the copy records which tablet), is recorded as signed on
a Tablet, an emailed one as Remote. The link is used up; the signed PDF is built and emailed afterwards.
When the template's text changed after the page was opened, nothing is signed
and the signer is asked to reload and read the new text. 10 calls an hour per
link and 300 per IP address.

**Auth (derived from code):** Guest — no session; the endpoint verifies the caller itself (HMAC signature, HTTP Basic credentials or a one-time token).

Source: `apps/ffl_core/ffl_core/agreements.py:1015`

post.summary: Count the drawer and close the day.
post.description:
Closes the open POS shifts, books any difference from the books and carries the count forward as tomorrow's opening.
A company's very first count sets the books to the physical drawer (against the bank) instead of booking a difference;
a later count first books any correction made since to the days before the first count (a true-up, also against
the bank), since that money was never in the drawer.

**Auth (derived from code):** Roles: Sales User / Sales Manager / Stock Manager / System Manager

Source: `apps/ffl_core/ffl_core/api/cash_drawer.py:154`

post.summary: Edit a pending counter order — the Pending Order page's Edit action.
post.description:
Cancels the submitted invoice (+ its Sales Orders) and rebuilds it through
create_order with the edited payload, in ONE transaction: editing is gated
to undisposed, never-pushed orders, so there are no FastBound/ShipStation/

anywhere in this flow.

refund_reference — same rules as cancel_order). A changed buyer refunds
the FULL paid amount to the ORIGINAL customer; the new invoice starts
unpaid.

back unchanged (same house, lane and quantity — the price may change) and
their Distributor Orders are re-pointed at the rebuilt invoice instead of
being ordered again. New lines are planned and ordered as usual, so adding an
item to an order already placed buys just that item.

post.summary: Build + insert + submit a Purchase Receipt from the page's payload.
post.description:
`payload` arrives as a JSON string when called via frappe.call from the
browser; accept dicts too for internal Python callers.

Schema:
        {
                "supplier": "ACME-FFL",
                "source": "RSR",                       # required — internal procurement channel
                "acquisition_type": "Purchase",        # optional — FastBound bound-book acquisition type
                "posting_date": "2026-05-05",          # optional, defaults to today
                "posting_time": "14:30:00",            # optional, defaults to now
                "warehouse": "Main - GS",              # optional, defaults to company default
                "notes": "...",                        # optional
                "items": [
                        {"item_code": "X", "qty": 100, "rate": 0.50, "serials": [], "service_need": 0},
                        {"item_code": "FIREARM-A", "qty": 1, "rate": 500, "serials": ["A001"],
                         "service_need": 1, "manufacturer": "Glock", "model_name": "19",
                         "firearm_type": "Pistol", "caliber": "9mm", "importer": ""},
                        {"item_code": "FIREARM-B", "qty": 1, "rate": 0, "serials": ["B001"],
                         "zero_cost_confirmed": 1, "zero_cost_reason": "Supplier gift",
                         "zero_cost_note": "", "manufacturer": "...", "model_name": "..."}
                ]
        }

Any line may carry ``storage_location`` (a Storage Location name): where the
units are put in the store. A firearm line with several serials fills that slot and
the next free ones in the same zone; ``serial_locations`` ({serial: location})
overrides it per gun. A line with no location lands in "unassigned" on the
Storage Locations page. Ignored for a customer-custody receive.

`rate` is REQUIRED on every line except a customer-custody receipt
(is_ffl_transfer, forced to 0 here) and a consignor's stock
(acquisition_type="Consignment", legitimately $0). A missing rate and a
rate of 0 are NOT the same thing and neither is accepted silently: an
acquisition that really was free must say so with `zero_cost_confirmed: 1`
plus a `zero_cost_reason` from ffl_core.setup.zero_cost.ZERO_COST_REASONS
("Supplier gift" / "Promotional item" / "Warranty replacement" / "Sample" /
"Other"), and "Other" additionally requires a free-text `zero_cost_note`.
The trio lands on the Purchase Receipt Item (ffl_-prefixed) and, for
firearms, on each Serial No.

Validation here is minimal — server-side hooks (validate, on_submit)
enforce the FFL gate + Used Firearm qty=1 + Acquisition creation.

A purchase from a private seller (``acquisition_source`` "Individual")
that costs anything says how the seller was paid: ``seller_payment_method``
(Cash / Zelle / Check / ACH) and, unless Cash, ``seller_payment_reference``
(check number, Zelle confirmation, ACH reference). Whether and how much is
paid is one decision (``cash_drawer.seller_payment_at_receipt``), the same
one ``seller_payment_preview`` gives the page before Submit. The payment is
booked in the receive's transaction BEFORE the bound-book push, and the
drawer lock is taken first, before any stock is written, with a bounded
wait (the same lock order as a count, so the two never deadlock): nothing
that can fail runs after FastBound has the acquisition, and a push that
fails rolls the payment back with the receipt. The amount booked must be
the amount the dialog showed, or the receive is refused before the push. Dr Stock Received But Not Billed / Cr Cash, or the bank account,
dated today (``cash_drawer.record_goods_payout``). It covers every line, the guns
included. Which receipts pay: ``cash_drawer.receipt_pays_seller`` (the
acquisition type blank, "Purchase" or "Individual"); a Consignment,
Gunsmithing or transfer receipt, a customer-custody one and a dealer
purchase pay nobody here, and a method sent for one is ignored.

post.summary: Create a Used Firearm Item + FFL Acquisition for an individual trade-in.
post.description:
With payload.apply_credit truthy, the acquisition is parked as a DRAFT
(booked at checkout submit) and the result carries `credit` — a locked
negative TRADE-IN-CREDIT line payload for the POS cart. Re-running the
dialog for a serial that already has a pending draft refreshes that
draft (new cost honoured) instead of duplicating it.

Without apply_credit the store buys the gun and pays the seller now:
payload.payout_method (Cash / Zelle / Check / ACH, and payout_reference
unless Cash) is required. The gun is received on a Purchase Receipt from
the seller, dated today, and the payment booked with it (Dr Stock Received
But Not Billed / Cr Cash or the bank) so the cash drawer count includes it
(_buy_now).

Accessories / ammo (payload.accessories, [{item_code, qty, rate}] with
rate the per-unit value) come in alone (has_firearm 0) or with the gun:
with apply_credit a draft Material Receipt and a credit line of their own
(_park_accessories), without it lines on the same paid receipt.

**Permissions:** roles.TRADE_IN_ROLES: the counter's sales role plus the stock roles; holding only the sales manager role is refused. A caller without a stock role files the gun under no Item (one is made for this gun) or an existing per-gun priced firearm Item (_check_counter_item); making or choosing any other Item stays a stock job. Everything behind the gate runs gate-free (firearm_intake.create_intake, receive_goods._create_receive), each of our writes with ignore_permissions; the ERPNext-internal checks against the session user (the gun's stock bundle) rest on the DocPerm setup/pos_compat.ROLE_GRANTS gives the counter.

post.description:
keeping the SAME Serial No and FFL Acquisition records — so the gun's price,
photos, condition, maker/importer/model/caliber, A&D history and FastBound
linkage all survive (nothing is deleted, so nothing can be dropped).

ERPNext ties a serial to one Item, so the stock moves with two ledger legs:
issue the serial out of the old Item, flip the serial's item_code, then receive
it into the target. The A&D record's `item` is re-pointed in place. FastBound is
NOT touched — reassign is a POS-internal re-bucketing; the bound book only changes
on an explicit serial edit. A per-gun WooCommerce listing, where the gun has one,
IS delisted: it belonged to the old Item, and leaving it live sells the same rifle
twice. Whitelisted for the Serial No form's "Reassign Item" action, for resolving
the sync's `regroup_needed` list, and for the Woo webhook's declared cross-Item

post.summary: Re-run the FastBound push for a submitted FFL Disposition that failed.
post.description:
``push_disposition_to_fastbound`` is a ``@frappe.task`` and nothing else —
there was no way to re-run one. A push that failed sat in
``fastbound_sync_error`` until the next daily ``reconcile_failed_pushes``,
which is up to 24 hours with a firearm out of the building and no bound-book
entry for it. DISP-2026-02000 spent a day in exactly that state while the
obstacle that caused the 400 had already been cleared by hand.

A thin wrapper on purpose: it re-checks who may press it and what may be
pressed, then calls the task unchanged. Run INLINE rather than enqueued so
the operator sees the outcome — the task is already idempotent (it no-ops on
an already-linked record) and carries its own retry/back-off.

The ``PUSHABLE_DISPOSITION_TYPES`` check is not decoration. A Retail Sale is
a 4473 disposition that FastBound's own wizard owns; pushing one from here
would book a to-individual transfer as a plain bound-book entry — a
compliance defect, not a sync error. The task would refuse it silently, so
this refuses it loudly instead of pretending to have done something. So does
FastBound being switched off, for the same reason: the task returns silently
on a disabled integration, which behind a button reads as "it failed again,
reason unknown".

The task's retry ladder is turned OFF here (``_retries=0``): an operator is
waiting, and the default four attempts with back-off can hold the desk for
~80 seconds before showing anything.

post.summary: Re-apply the serial WooCommerce still holds to rows stuck on a STALE
post.description:
``reservation_error``.

A rejection is a snapshot of the moment it was written ("that gun is held by
WOO-ORD-x"). The only thing that ever retried it was the next
``order.updated`` webhook — so when the obstacle cleared (the other order
cancelled, or swapped to a different gun) nothing re-ran, and a Woo order that
has gone ``completed`` sends no further webhook. The row then sat in the
Pending Order queue indefinitely, quoting a reason that had stopped being
true, and staff had no way to clear it but to re-save the serial on Woo.
(2026-08-07: WOO-ORD-01488 was refused C2322, which WOO-ORD-01491 released
eight minutes later; only an unrelated update two hours on unstuck it.)

Whitelisted so staff can run it on demand rather than waiting out the cron —
which also gives the aged-out orders below a manual way back in.

Bounded on every axis, because this is an unattended writer that calls an
external store:

* ``LIMIT`` per run, oldest first;
* orders older than ``_RETRY_MAX_AGE_DAYS`` are reported **once** and then
  left alone — a sweep that retries forever is how a permanent failure turns
  into permanent noise (the lesson ``_fb_error_is_terminal`` encodes);
* out-of-stock rejections are excluded outright: no dealer serial exists on
  Woo to re-apply, so re-reading that order could never fix it;
* per-site ``auto_sync_enabled`` gate, one Settings read per site.

post.summary: Single WooCommerce webhook entry point (guest, HMAC-verified).
post.description:
**Auth (derived from code):** Guest — no session; the endpoint verifies the caller itself (HMAC signature, HTTP Basic credentials or a one-time token).

**Payload:** WooCommerce's webhook JSON body; the X-WC-Webhook-Topic header selects the handler (order.created/updated, product.*, ...). The X-WC-Webhook-Signature header must carry a valid HMAC over the raw body (secret configured in Woo Sync Settings).

Source: `apps/ffl_woo_sync/ffl_woo_sync/woocommerce/webhook.py:2833`

200.description: 200 with a minimal JSON body ({ok, topic/handled/error}) on success. 400 when ``?site=`` names a store this POS does not run (only the retail store is connected) and 401 when HMAC verification fails — the two cases that mean "stop delivering here", which is what a 4xx gets WooCommerce to do; the order is not read or processed for either. Every other outcome logs (where there is anything worth logging) and returns 200, so WooCommerce does not retry or auto-disable the webhook over something the caller cannot fix.
